articles.title: Rains slow down across Andhra Pradesh after two days of havoc
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The rainfall activity, triggered by the Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’, has slowed down in Andhra Pradesh on Thursday, (November 5, 2026) after two days of havoc and leaving at least four perons dead, three in Bapatla district and one in Guntur district.

Between 8.30 a.m. and 2 p.m. on Thursday, only the district of SPSR Nellore recorded widespread moderate showers of around 55 mm. Other places in the districts of Tirupati, Anakapalli, Prakasam, recorded light showers till noon.

Light showers may continue on November 6, but after that, there may be a brief pause in the rainfall activity in the State. According to the India Meteorological Department’s forecast for the next seven days until November 12, the State may not see widespread rainfall, but it has said isolated heavy rainfall, at one or two places, in coastal A.P. is likely during the next seven days.

As per a release from the State Emergency Operations Centre of the Real Time Governance Society, reservoirs and drains are now stable, and that inflows are declining. Prakasam Barrage is discharging the same quantity as it is receiving. Thammileru and Budameru, which were rising on Wednesday, are now falling. Yerra Kalva, which had seen a sharp rise on Wednesday night, has also stabilised. Kondaveeti Vagu pump house is being operated to keep levels under control.
While the cyclone impact has largely subsided, the RTGS officials advised people in low-lying areas and near drains, canals and reservoirs to remain cautious.

On November 3 and 4, the districts of Palnadu, West Godavari, Bapatla, East Godavari, Kakinada, Eluru recorded very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall due to the cyclone. Except for Palnadu, which still has a deficit of 26.7%, the deficits in the other five districts have been covered after the reecnt spell of rains.

While the northern and Central parts of the State benefitted from the heavy rainfall caused by the two back-to-back cyclones of Arnab and Murasu, the region of Rayalaseema continues to wait for rain. Sri Sathy Sai is the worst hit, with 56% deficit, followed by Kurnool that has a deficit of 51.5%. Prakasam, which received good rain in the past two days, still has a deficit of 50.8%. Nandyal, Anantapur, YSR Kadapa and Annamayya have deficits between 40% and 50%, while Chittoor has a deficit of 32.4% and Tirupati 21.4%.

articles.title: Climate change increased tropical Cyclone Arnab’s damage by 33%: Study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Climate change increased the damage caused by the tropical Cyclone Arnab, which struck eastern India on October 28, by 33%, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in additional direct economic losses compared to a pre-industrial climate baseline, according to a new study.
ALSO WATCH Cyclone Arnab batters east coast: 5 dead in Andhra Pradesh, 17 Odisha districts affected
It added that the storm brought intense rain, peak 1-minute sustained winds of up to 202 kilometres per hour, and severe damage to infrastructure across Andhra Pradesh.
The study was carried out by researchers at the Imperial College London’s Grantham Institute and published on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

For their analysis, researchers used the Imperial College Storm Model (IRIS) to simulate Cyclone Arnab under current conditions (plus 1.3° Celsius above pre-industrial levels) versus a counterfactual climate without human-induced warming.
“Climate change increased Cyclone Arnab’s maximum wind speed by approximately 5%, and intensified its eyewall rainfall rate by 11% at landfall,” according to the study.

It also revealed that direct damage to physical assets in India was estimated to be 33% higher than it would have been in a pre-industrial climate baseline, attributing roughly 25% of the total economic damage directly to climate change.
ALSO WATCH Beyond Cyclone Arnab: can India tackle the growing cost of natural disasters? | Insight India

In a statement, Dr. Nathan Sparks, researcher at the Department of Physics, Imperial College London, said: “These findings are a powerful reminder of the price of inaction. The costs of climate change are not hypothetical future projections — they are hitting coastal communities in eastern India today.”

articles.title: Andhra local body polls: Clashes erupt between YSRCP, TDP groups in Kadapa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Amid ZPTC and MPTC elections, clashes broke out between YSRCP and TDP activists in several areas of Kadapa district on Thursday morning. Two groups of people have attacked each other with petrol bombs in Yerripalli village in Pulivendla mandal of the district.

According to sources, a quarrel started among the agents of YSRCP and TDP while sitting near a polling station in Yerripalli. The groups of both political parties have argued and exchanged harsh words. Meanwhile, some of them reportedly hurled petrol bombs. None were injured in the clash.

Speaking to The Hindu , Pulivendla Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Murali Nayak clarified, “The activists of both parties used firecrackers, which were brought to celebrate after victory, to attack each other. They took out petrol from their bikes to escalate the fight.”

“However, the police forces controlled them within five minutes. Such incidents took place near polling stations in R. Thummalapalli Parnapalli villages in Pulivendla mandal, but the police staff immediately calmed down the situation in these areas respectively,” he informed.

The clashes reportedly happened after Kadapa MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy toured those polling stations. The TDP workers have alleged that the YSRCP leader encouraged his party cadre to create violence with a fear of failure in ZPTC/ MPTC elections similar to Municipal polls.

Not only in Pulivendula, incidents of pelting stones were reported in Gundlakunta village in Jammalamadugu constituency and Nandalur village in Rajampeta division. The clashes were also witnessed in Chintarajupalli, Railway Kodur and Badvel areas.

District SP Shelke Nachiket Vishwanath visited the polling stations in Vemula mandal and inspected the security arrangements on the ground. He instructed the police personnel to remain vigilant and ensure that the elections are conducted in a peaceful and impartial manner.

The polling for 16 ZPTC and 55 MPTC constituencies commenced in the district at 7 am. Special security arrangements have been made at 167 highly sensitive, 134 sensitive and five problematic polling stations. Except few areas, the voting was peaceful with 48.92% turnout by 1 pm

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi was born in family of Prime Ministers, he is not after PM post but nation’s interests: Jagga Reddy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Reacting to Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s comment that Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi can never become the Prime Minister, Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) working president T. Jagga Reddy reminded that Mr. Gandhi was born in the family of Prime Ministers and he was not after the post but the nation’s interests.

Addressing a press conference at Gandhi Bhavan in Hyderabad on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), Mr. Jagga Reddy said the Prime Minister’s post had always been within the reach of the Nehru-Gandhi family and Mr. Rahul Gandhi could have become Prime Minister in 2004 and in 2009 itself had he wanted the position.

Mr. Rahul Gandhi is not after the Prime Minister’s position like others in the Bharatiya Janata (BJP), Mr. Jagga Reddy said adding that Telangana Congress was ready to take up Mr. Shah’s comments as a challenge and work towards winning all 17 Lok Sabha seats in the State in the next parliamentary elections.

Referring to the BJP’s invocation of Lord Ram in its political campaigns, he said Mahatma Gandhi had sung Raghupati Raghava Raja Ram during the freedom movement, at a time when neither the BJP nor its leaders Narendra Modi and Amit Shah was born.

He said the BJP was always busy claiming exclusive ownership of Lord Ram’s name, pointing out that the Congress and Mahatma Gandhi had invoked Ram in their public life long before the BJP came into existence. Mr. Jagga Reddy said the BJP had come to power and the Prime Minister had secured three terms by invoking Lord Ram’s name, but was not following the ideals and path shown by the Lord.

articles.title: Cheranalloor luxury car crash: court upholds teen’s bail, raps police and prosecution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Additional District and Sessions Court designated to try cases involving atrocities against women and children in Ernakulam, Keralam, on Thursday (November 5, 2026) dismissed the appeals seeking suspension of the bail granted to the 17-year-old involved in the Cheranalloor crash case that claimed a life, while coming down heavily on the police and prosecution.

Judge Kavitha Gangadharan questioned the very basis for the registration of the FIR against the teenager in conflict with law, pointing out that such registration is warranted only in offences carrying a punishment of seven years’ imprisonment or more. The multiple alterations made to the FIR also came in for criticism. The police were accused of showing scant regard for the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, with the court questioning the absence of the social background report mandated in cases involving juveniles. The court even read out the relevant provisions of the Act to the investigation officer, an Assistant Commissioner with the Crime Branch.
The court observed that the police are not expected to act beyond the law even under pressure. The judge also asked the prosecution to show reason for not imposing fine while dismissing the appeals.

Earlier, the court had directed the investigation officer to submit within an hour details of FIRs registered in the district or elsewhere in the State in connection with accidents involving juvenile drivers in which Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which prescribes punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder, had been invoked.

The court sought the data to append it to the order on the appeals filed by the prosecution and the family of the deceased against the bail granted to the teenager by the Juvenile Justice Board. She warned that the investigation officer would be held answerable if no FIRs had been registered elsewhere invoking BNS Section 105 in similar cases and if the provision had been invoked only in the present case. Though the officer submitted details of nine accident cases involving juveniles in the district, Section 105 had not been invoked in any of them.

The court was also critical of the investigating agency for filing the appeal against the bail in the wrong court instead of the court designated to try cases involving juveniles, the only such court in the district. The judge also sought to know from the prosecution whether it had any doubt that the Juvenile Justice Model Rules constituted the sole State government framework governing matters involving children in conflict with law.
Bhadrakeerthi R.J., daughter of the victim Jayabalakrishnan, expressed dismay over the verdict, which she said she “could not comprehend.”

“It was dramatic and full of twists. People of Keralam will have no faith in the courts any more. We were expecting a favourable verdict both from this court and the High Court, (which granted anticipatory bail to the judicial officer, the father of the juvenile accused). Issues that had never been raised until today were brought up by the court. However, we will continue our fight,” she said outside the court.

articles.title: KTR questions BJP’s inaction on alleged ‘RR tax’ collection
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president K.T. Rama Rao asked whether Union Home Minister Amit Shah will only level allegations of ‘RR Tax’ or has any plan to take against Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy since the allegations are regularly made.

In a post on social media platforms, KTR questioned the Bharatiiya Janata Party (BJP) leadership at the Centre over its failure to act on allegations and claimed it reflected the Congress and BJP of having an understanding that protects each other.

He alleged that ₹200 was being collected per square foot in the name of ‘RR tax’ and said the practice was widely known in the real estate sector. Let the statements not be limited to rhetoric but take concrete action against the alleged collections, he said.

Taking a dig at the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, KTR said, “Bada bhai Modi will never take action against his ABVP chhota bhai Revanth.” An understanding between the BJP and Congress was behind the Centre’s inaction, he claimed.

fullParagraphs: From the poverty income ruler line provided by the recent World Bank estimates, India has recorded one of the fastest extreme income-poverty declines in the world, as per its latest Poverty and Equity brief, which highlights that between 2011 and 2023, an estimated 496 million people moved out of poverty, with extreme income-based poverty ($3/per day) declining to 2.6%.

For the same period, the share of the population living below the lower middle-income country line ($4.20/day, 2021 PPP) fell from 57.7% to 16.1%. Non-monetary poverty indicators, as per OPHI’s Multi-dimensional Poverty Index, also recorded a sharp reduction in overall poverty numbers, i.e., from 53.8% in 2005-06 to 16.4% in 2019-21.

articles.title: U.S. midterm elections: An economy under pressure, political shift and the road ahead
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The 2026 U.S. midterm elections have dealt a significant political setback to President Donald Trump, with Democrats securing control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. Beyond their political implications, the results raise important questions about the future direction of the world’s largest economy, particularly as American households grapple with rising living costs, persistent inflation and high borrowing expenses.

The election has highlighted a contradiction in the U.S. economy. Although real GDP expanded at an annualised rate of 3.4% in Q3 2026, a substantial section of the population remains dissatisfied with its financial circumstances. Inflation accelerated to 3.7% in September, up from 3.4% in August, largely driven by rising energy costs. Fuel oil prices surged 74.2%, compared with 52% previously, adding to household financial pressures.

fullParagraphs: Indian shares are expected to open higher on Thursday (November 5, 2026), as crude oil prices slumped to a two-month low ​as investors bet that Democrats’ victory in US midterm elections could hasten ‌the end of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.
GIFT ​Nifty futures were at 24,295.5 as of ⁠8:01 a.m. IST, indicating a positive start for the benchmark Nifty 50 , which closed at 23,960.6 on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).

Foreign investors bought Indian shares worth ‌₹72.84 billion ($769.65 million) on Wednesday (November 4, 2026, as per provisional data. This marks their fourth straight session of buying, ‌suggesting they may be returning to India after a ‌strong ⁠sell-off this year.
Brent crude futures dropped 1% to $93.5 per ⁠barrel, after an 8.7% slide in the previous session.

U.S. and European stocks rallied on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) after Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress in ​the US midterm elections, providing greater ‌political clarity and reducing uncertainty that has weighed on markets.

Democrats’ win is being seen as a scathing rebuke to President Donald Trump, whose administration’s global tariff policy and decision to ‌go to war in the Middle East also contributed ​to the Indian market’s underperformance this year.

The domestic markets are now showing signs of a recovery. Indian ⁠benchmark Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex have risen 5.6% in the last five sessions, in their longest winning streak in nearly ‌five months, aided by foreign buying, easing oil prices, and strong earnings.

“Unlike the earlier gradual decline (in oil prices), the magnitude of this move can materially improve India’s near-term macro and earnings outlook if sustained,” said Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, founder and CEO of research advisory firm HST Wealth.

articles.title: Centre earmarks ₹2,814 crore to boost lithium, nickel processing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a ₹2,814-crore capital expenditure support scheme to establish domestic processing facilities for lithium and nickel, seeking to strengthen India’s critical mineral ecosystem and reduce import dependence. The scheme will remain in force for five years.

India’s domestic beneficiation and processing infrastructure for critical minerals remains limited, with commercial-scale operations constrained by high capital requirements, limited access to suitable technologies and inadequate availability of raw materials, the government said in a statement.
Union Minister for Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy said the scheme would strengthen domestic capabilities, boost manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports.

“It will benefit key sectors such as electronics, semiconductors, batteries, defence, heavy equipment and machinery, while supporting industries across the manufacturing value chain that utilise critical minerals,” he said in a social media post.
Under the scheme, the government will provide a capital subsidy of 30% of the investment required to establish four critical mineral processing plants — two each for lithium and nickel.
The minimum processing capacity will be 30,000 tonnes (30 kt) each for lithium and 50,000 tonnes (50 kt) each for nickel.
The subsidy will be capped at ₹500 crore per beneficiary for lithium projects and ₹900 crore per beneficiary for nickel facilities.

The four beneficiaries will be selected through a least-cost bidding process, with preference given to technically qualified applicants seeking the lowest capital expenditure support. Incentives will be disbursed in three tranches.

Industry body the Federation of Indian Mineral Industries (FIMI) welcomed the initiative, saying it could encourage fresh investments, increase domestic value addition and strengthen supply chains for battery manufacturing and other strategic industries.
However, it said that securing adequate raw materials would be critical to the scheme’s success.
“Ensuring a reliable supply of raw material through domestic mining and overseas sourcing will be equally important for the success of these processing facilities,” the industry body told The Hindu.
It also underlined the need to develop the entire value chain, from mining to processing and refining, to strengthen India’s long-term mineral security.

articles.title: Union Cabinet approves new VISTAR scheme to overhaul India’s statistical system
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a ₹4,371 crore scheme to overhaul the statistical architecture of the country at both the Central as well as State level, called the Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR) scheme, for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31.

“Aligned with the central objective of Viksit Bharat 2047, the VISTAR Scheme is designed to establish a dynamic, real-time and future-ready official statistical architecture for enhanced timeliness, data granularity, interoperability with harmonised and AI ready datasets,” the government said in a release.

As per the government, the VISTAR scheme will be divided into three components: Comprehensive statistical operations and strengthening of the ecosystem, Support for statistical strengthening, and an Economic Census.

Under the Comprehensive Statistical Operations and Strengthening of Ecosystem component, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has proposed to conduct 59 surveys during the 16th Finance Commission cycle, as compared to 43 major surveys conducted previously.
This, the government said, could potentially fill “critical data gaps in various sectors” and thereby improve decision-making and enable timely and targeted policy interventions.

“In addition, building on recent digital transformations in technology enabled data collection and user-centric dissemination, MoSPI will focus on the end-to-end digitalisation of statistical processes and embedding Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning into regular workflows, primarily for data processing, validation, and analysis,” the government added.

Further, it added that, by mainstreaming alternate sources such as mobile phones, scanners, and e-commerce data, MoSPI will aim to complement traditional surveys, reduce respondent burden, fill data gaps, and strengthen evidence-based policymaking.

Under the support for statistical strengthening (SSS) component, the Centre will provide funds to State governments to help transform the statistical capabilities of States and Union Territories through a redesigned, deliverable-linked framework.

“The vision focuses on building state-level capacity to generate high-quality, granular data at the district and other disaggregated levels, developing indigenous data processing capabilities, and embedding data use cases into localized policymaking,” the government said.

MoSPI will also undertake the 8th Economic Census (EC) in collaboration with the States and Union Territories in order to obtain granular data and activity details of all the non-farm establishments and workers hired down to the gram panchayat and ward levels

This, the government said, would provide an assessment of the unorganised sector of the economy and will serve as the baseline for developing the National Statistical Business Register (SBR) to facilitate targeted enterprise surveys and strategic interventions.

“The economic census data will be extremely useful for planners and policy makers at national and sub-national levels, which will pave the way for estimating the contribution of the unorganised sector to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP),” the government said.

articles.title: Union Cabinet approves ₹14,500 crore VGF scheme to develop large scale energy storage in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Union Cabinet has approved a ₹14,500 crore Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme for the development of grid-scale energy storage systems for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31, the government announced on Wednesday.
According to the government, the scheme is aimed at supporting the development of 92 GWh of fresh, yet-to-be-commissioned, energy storage capacity across the country.

“The scheme will support creation of new capacities equivalent to 170% of the present-day grid scale energy storage system capacity in the country and help meet the required grid scale ESS capacity of 411 GWh by 2031-32,” the government said in a release.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Can battery storage save India’s renewable energy grid? | Business Matters

The scheme is designed to provide for the development of 60 GWh of hydro pumped storage plant (PSP) capacity, 30 GWh of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity and 2 GWh of capacity through alternative energy storage technologies, with a total estimated investment of ₹97,600 crore.

“The VGF support will help improve the financial viability of these projects and accelerate the deployment of large-scale energy storage infrastructure in the country,” the government said, adding that the scheme will also provide an impetus to domestic manufacturing of battery energy storage systems.

As per the government’s release, energy storage capacity will be allocated through a tariff-based competitive bidding process with both public and private sector electricity distribution companies eligible for VGF support for BESS and hydro PSP projects.
Projects based on alternative energy storage technologies, too, will be implemented by public and private sector entities.

“To promote indigenous manufacturing, BESS projects will be subject to a minimum Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) of 40%,” the government added. “The requirement will encourage domestic manufacturing, create opportunities for Indian industry and complement existing supply-side incentives for battery manufacturing.”

articles.title: What the BJP should learn from Trump’s redistricting failure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has lessons to draw from the Republican Party in the United States in its attempts to undertake a hurried, hushed and partisan redrawing of the country’s electoral map. The BJP has been planning for an out-of-cycle Census and a delimitation exercise by delaying the 2021 Census until 2026. The Republican Party redrew Congressional district boundaries across eight States under the direction of President Donald J. Trump in the hope of flipping seats currently held by Democrats. But they lost most of them and, in addition, lost seats they had hoped to retain, as their heartlands such as Texas and Florida slipped away.

Gerrymandering, the practice of redrawing electoral boundaries by packing or cracking particular social groups, assumes that voting preferences remain unchanged between election cycles. But when the traditional supporters of a party turn against it, constituency maps matter little. The Bankipur by-election in Bihar in August had proved the same point. The constituency is perfectly tailored for a BJP victory, going by its demographic composition. But when the upper-caste supporters of the party changed their minds, the BJP was decimated.

articles.title: U.S. midterm elections witness historic firsts: First Black woman governor to first Muslim senator
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The U.S. midterm elections 2026 will be remembered not just for the stunning number of losses Democrats handed to President Donald Trump and Republicans, but also for a wave of historic firsts across the country.

The closely watched polls, held on November 3, 2026, saw voters electing the first Native American female governor, the first Black female governor, the first Muslim US senator and first openly gay male US senator. The astonishing blue wave also means the United States will likely have its first-ever Black speaker of the House.

Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms reacts at a campaign office, the day after winning Georgia's race for governor and becoming the first Black woman elected governor of a US state during the US midterm elections in Atlanta, Georgia, US, November 4, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters

Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms was elected governor of Georgia, making history as the first Black woman to be elected governor in the United States, defeating Republican businessman Rick Jackson and flipping the top job in a key swing state. Her win returns the Governor’s office to Democrats after more than two decades of Republican control.
Democrat Deb Haaland answers questions during an interview at her campaign headquarters in Albuquerque. File photo | Photo Credit: AP

Democrat Deb Haaland became the first Native American female governor in U.S. history when was declared the winner over Republican Gregg Hull, a former mayor, to lead New Mexico. In 2018, Haaland was one of the first two Native American women elected to Congress. Then she became the first Native American Cabinet secretary, running President Joe Biden’s Department of the Interior.
Democrat Abdul El-Sayed speaks at an election night event on November 4, 2026, in Detroit, as his wife Sarah Jukaku watches. | Photo Credit: AP

Abdul El-Sayed will become the first Muslim American to serve in the U.S. Senate after registering victory in Michigan. The race between the progressive Michigan Democrat and Republican Mike Rogers had grabbed attention nationally. El-Sayed has had to contend with Republicans all the way up to Trump implying or overtly stating that the Michigan-born epidemiologist is not American and supports terrorism. El-Sayed and his supporters have denounced the attacks as Islamophobic or racist affronts to religious freedom.
Democratic Senate candidate Rep. Chris Pappas, right, speaks at an election night event, with Vann Bentley on November 3, 2026, in Manchester. | Photo Credit: AP Photo

Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas won his U.S. Senate race in New Hampshire and will become the country’s first openly gay male senator. He defeated former U.S. Sen. John E. Sununu, a Republican who previously served in both chambers of Congress.
Democrat Peggy Flanagan, speaks at an election night event on November 3, 2026, in St. Paul. | Photo Credit: AP photo

Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan has become the first Native American female U.S. senator, helping Democrats win back the Senate. A citizen of the White Earth Band of Ojibwe, Flanagan defeated Republican Michele Tafoya, a former NFL sideline reporter.

fullParagraphs: Following the drubbing of U.S. President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the midterm elections, Iranians set fire to a giant poster featuring the American leader and his allies at a rally in Tehran.
The cheering audience waved red flags to demand revenge for Khamenei’s death.
“We will kill Trump,” read the slogan on some of the flags waved by the crowd as a song named “We Must Rise” mourning Khamenei blared from nearby speakers.

As Washington navigates the fallout from a sweeping Republican electoral defeat, Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the U.S., Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has launched a blistering critique of American leadership, accusing officials of bringing “losing gambler energy” to the table while America teeters on an “Israel-First cliff”.

In a post on X, Mr. Ghalibaf wrote, “Losing gambler energy, can’t walk away from the table. Boss is prepping the next war phase while America teeters on an Israel-First cliff. Skip the TED talk. Why not say this to your boss?”

Democrats vowed to use their resounding midterm victory to rein in President Donald Trump, setting up two years of possible deadlock in Washington, as Mr. Trump spent his first post-election appearance showing off his under-construction White House ballroom.
It will be the first time ⁠that Mr. Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress.
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Wednesday (November 4) that the incoming majority would be focused on affordability and accountability.

Mr. Trump’s announcement showed that even the Republican President, who moved the American embassy to Jerusalem in his first term, cracked down on pro-Palestine protests at home and launched a war, along with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, against Iran, recognised the growing electoral liability of unconditional support for Israel.

The midterm results could accelerate this political churn. The Democrats have secured control of both the House and the Senate. The election was fought largely on domestic issues, particularly the economy and the cost of living, but the war on Iran and its impact on the economy, particularly fuel prices, also figured in the Republican setback. Mr. Trump himself acknowledged that the war had hurt his party.
Vice President J.D. Vance, in a lengthy social media post , blamed the war for the defeat and one of the four suggestions made to gain back the ground was to “change our relationship to Israel”.
U.S.-Israel ties face renewed strain as midterms shift political dynamics, domestic debates, and bipartisan scrutiny of support.

articles.title: The war that defeated ‘America First’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: U.S. Vice-President J.D. Vance has supplied the most politically damaging explanation of the Republican mid-term debacle: “The reason we lost is the war.” His assessment deserves attention because it identifies a contradiction at the heart of Donald Trump’s presidency. An administration elected in large part on promises to avoid costly foreign entanglements made the U.S. a participant in another West Asian war without evidence that it advanced American interests. Republicans have now paid a huge electoral price for that reversal.

Mr. Vance’s explanation goes beyond the familiar claim that disappointed supporters stayed home. He argues that former Trump voters crossed over to the Democrats. He identified four demands among these defectors: ending the war, addressing living costs, putting American interests first, and changing Washington’s relationship with Israel. The political significance of his diagnosis is unmistakable. The administration’s own second-in-command has connected Republican losses to the collision between its nationalist promises and its foreign policy.

articles.title: Sarah Jukaku: First Muslim U.S. senator’s wife has a Karnataka link
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Sarah Jukaku, a doctor and wife of Democrat Abdul EI-Sayed , who is the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate in the midterm elections, traces her family roots to Bhatkal in Uttara Kannada district, of Karnataka, according to media reports.

Dr. Sarah is the granddaughter of the late J.H. Shamsuddin Jukaku, a lawyer from Bhatkal who served as Deputy Finance Minister in the erstwhile Mysore State government, led by the then Chief Minister B.D. Jatti, in the late 1950s and early 1960s. Shamsuddin was also the Deputy Minister for Electricity in the then government led by then Chief Minister S. Nijalingappa, reports said.

articles.title: Climate change increased tropical Cyclone Arnab’s damage by 33%: Study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Climate change increased the damage caused by the tropical Cyclone Arnab, which struck eastern India on October 28, by 33%, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in additional direct economic losses compared to a pre-industrial climate baseline, according to a new study.
ALSO WATCH Cyclone Arnab batters east coast: 5 dead in Andhra Pradesh, 17 Odisha districts affected
It added that the storm brought intense rain, peak 1-minute sustained winds of up to 202 kilometres per hour, and severe damage to infrastructure across Andhra Pradesh.
The study was carried out by researchers at the Imperial College London’s Grantham Institute and published on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

For their analysis, researchers used the Imperial College Storm Model (IRIS) to simulate Cyclone Arnab under current conditions (plus 1.3° Celsius above pre-industrial levels) versus a counterfactual climate without human-induced warming.
“Climate change increased Cyclone Arnab’s maximum wind speed by approximately 5%, and intensified its eyewall rainfall rate by 11% at landfall,” according to the study.

It also revealed that direct damage to physical assets in India was estimated to be 33% higher than it would have been in a pre-industrial climate baseline, attributing roughly 25% of the total economic damage directly to climate change.
ALSO WATCH Beyond Cyclone Arnab: can India tackle the growing cost of natural disasters? | Insight India

In a statement, Dr. Nathan Sparks, researcher at the Department of Physics, Imperial College London, said: “These findings are a powerful reminder of the price of inaction. The costs of climate change are not hypothetical future projections — they are hitting coastal communities in eastern India today.”

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: The Amazon is no longer a carbon sink, it is an emitter
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The world’s largest tropical forest, referred to as the ‘lungs of the planet,’ the Amazon rainforest once acted as a vast carbon sink that helped absorb human-induced CO2 emissions. But now, a study startlingly finds that the Amazon releases more CO2 than it absorbs from the atmosphere, as it is decimated by deforestation and forest fires.

Scientists measured CO2 levels at different atmospheric altitudes, using research airplanes, between the years 2010 and 2024 at four Amazonian sites. Their findings indicated that “Amazonia is a net carbon source rather than a sink and cannot offset regional anthropogenic emissions.”

articles.title: Mobile phone retailers expect 10% price hike post Diwali even as sales drop
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Mainstream mobile phone retailers are experiencing a footfall and sales contraction of 25% to 35% in value-oriented categories. Furthermore, major Android handset makers are expecting a 10% price hike shortly after Diwali .

All India Mobile Retail Association (AIMRA) projects a staggering 50% volume drop after mid-Novmber that could persist over an extended period. In response to flagging demand and severe component constraints, top smartphone brands have already cut production schedules by 30%, the retail body said.
The festive season, beginning with Navratri and concluding after Diwali, is a crucial time for Indian mobile retailers. This period sees stores brimming with customers.
Retailers are facing a subdued festive market characterised by declining footfall, plummeting sales of mass-market devices and rising costs due to a global memory chip shortage.

The sub-₹20,000 smartphone segment has been the worst hit — a category that traditionally brought in volume sales. But retailers report that this segment is crippled as leading brands have not put out any lineup of viable 5G handsets.
Historic price hikes of entry-level models, depreciating rupee and drop in purchasing power of rural consumers have paralysed the sub-₹20,000 smartphone segment.
Major original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) have signalled that future entry-level 5G pricing will start exclusively from ₹25,000 upwards, shutting out budget-conscious consumers.

With device prices climbing relentlessly, financing has become the primary driver of retail sales as 80% of smartphone purchases are supported by EMI financing. Retailers have requested smartphone brands and NBFC partners to introduce structured long-tenure, zero-down-payment schemes to sustain demand and drive volume conversions for high-ticket devices priced above ₹75,000.

“Underpinning these consumer price hikes is an aggressive global memory chip supply tightening engineered by chip manufacturers. AIMRA has strongly urged the World Trade Organisation (WTO) and Ministers of Commerce and Industry across key global economies to immediately establish a multilateral regulatory watchdog to rein in artificial price manipulation. Without urgent intervention, skyrocketing device costs threaten to permanently break the mobile replacement cycle, forcing consumers to hold onto their phones for extended multi-year periods,” said Kailash Lakhyani, founding chairman and president of AIMRA.

articles.title: Helping hand: On Cyclones Arnab and Murasu
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Long-term preparedness and a swift response by authorities minimised casualties when the back-to-back cyclones Arnab and Murasu hit two places of the Andhra Pradesh coast. In Andhra Pradesh, damage from Cyclone Arnab , which made landfall on October 28 was estimated at roughly ₹4,526 crore. Initial estimates of the damage by Cyclone Murasu, which crossed the coast on November 3, indicate that about 52,500 hectares of standing crops were affected. The State reported 12 deaths from the two cyclones. The first cyclone damaged nearly 90,000 hectares of standing crops in southern parts of Odisha. After preliminary on-the-spot assessment of flood-hit areas, the Union government is expected to soon release the first instalment of funds to the affected States. Personnel from Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu have also gone to the rescue of Andhra Pradesh.

The deployment of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) and other technologies has significantly reduced human casualties and property damage. During Cyclone Hudhud in October 2014, Andhra Pradesh reported 63 deaths and damage estimated at nearly ₹22,000 crore. As natural disasters become more frequent in India, greater collaboration is needed between higher learning institutions, especially in science and technology, and central and State government agencies. Authorities must develop an effective compensation framework for saving crops/crop losses. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, a crop insurance scheme that was launched by the Union government a decade ago, has not provided farmers with comprehensive safety cover, as they suffer due to the vagaries of nature. The Union government should improve the scheme so that all farmers are encouraged to bring their crops under the scheme, while State governments should raise awareness about the insurance scheme and support agriculturists by topping up benefits that are under the insurance cover. The Centre should also focus on financial assistance for permanent restoration projects. The initial stand of the Union government was that the National and State Disaster Response Funds were meant for response and relief, not recovery and reconstruction, but following the 15th Finance Commission’s nudge, it added recovery and reconstruction as a component of the two funds two years ago. However, when public infrastructure suffers extensive damage, the Centre should provide additional assistance to ease the burden on affected States. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his team at the Centre must act in the spirit of “cooperative federalism”.

articles.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

articles.title: Coming of age: On the Binance hack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself . Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack.

So, Binance used a stable source of revenue to finance an emergency fund, which it deployed when an emergency occurred. The system worked perfectly, also showing how maturely and responsibly the crypto space can be run. The Indian government and the Reserve Bank of India still view the private crypto space as the Wild West of techno-finance. This is no longer the case. Large crypto companies are employing prudential practices, safeguarding customers, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies. If the fear is that cryptocurrencies are not backed by any asset, then Indian policymakers can choose to allow only stablecoins, which do have real assets underpinning them. Indians are not at higher risk from cryptos than they are from fake stock market scams. The best defence is awareness. By refusing to regulate the crypto space in India and, indeed, taxing it at a prohibitive rate, the government is driving Indians towards either the black market, where such scams proliferate, or foreign exchanges. The government can take a leaf out of Binance’s book and mandate an industry-maintained emergency fund. There is ample international legislation to emulate now. The point is, crypto risks have fallen and adoption is rising. Now is the time to regulate the industry.

articles.title: Business, unusual: On engaging with the Myanmar junta
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Months after a sham election that installed junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as Myanmar’s civilian President, the military continues to wage war on its own people even as the world has largely looked away. More than a lakh people are estimated to have died since the 2021 coup, many in fighting between the junta and the anti-coup People’s Defence Forces and ethnic armed organisations. The junta has also killed thousands of civilians in air strikes on villages in rebel-held areas to terrorise communities into giving up their resistance. With wars affecting Ukraine, Gaza, Sudan and Yemen, and Iran, the world has grown numb to such violence. The junta has exploited that indifference and a shifting geopolitical situation to act with impunity. Russia and China, its principal arms suppliers, have stood by it with the former supplying jets that were used to bomb civilians. Beijing, which tacitly allowed three ethnic armed organisations to launch an offensive in Shan and Rakhine States in late 2023, has since pressured two of them into ceasefires and returning seized territory. It also backed the January election. Since being sworn in, Min Aung Hlaing has visited India , Thailand, Vietnam and three other ASEAN member-states. ASEAN still swears by its Five-Point Consensus, which calls for an end to violence and dialogue. Yet, its members seem more than eager to do business with a regime that has flouted every point. Meanwhile, U.S. officials reportedly held secret talks with the junta in Tokyo in June and October, and a senior delegation met Min Aung Hlaing in Naypyidaw in September. Japan is reportedly pressing the Financial Action Task Force to take Myanmar off its blacklist.

The motives are not hard to understand. China wants an outlet to the Indian Ocean and security for its oil and gas pipelines. It has also played both sides, dealing with the junta and powerful rebel groups such as the Kachin Independence Organisation, whose territory is rich in rare earths and jade, and the United Wa State Army, which runs a massive tin mine. New Delhi wants to revive its stalled Act East policy, including the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project. The U.S. eyes access to mining vital heavy rare earths such as dysprosium and terbium, for use in electric vehicles and weapons systems. What these short-sighted overtures miss is that trade thrives in a country at peace, not one where armed groups are perennially battling for control. The junta which has killed its citizens and has scuttled every move towards democracy cannot deliver that peace. Unless the generals are made to answer for their war crimes, Myanmar will remain a war zone. It will be ruinous not only for its hapless people but also for businesses seeking to trade with it.

articles.title: United stand: On protests against SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The gathering of hundreds of thousands of people at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, organised by the Congress-led INDIA bloc parties, was a milestone in the battle for the restoration of the integrity of India’s election process. As more and more skeletons tumble out the of the closet of the Election Commission of India (ECI), its chief Gyanesh Kumar has chosen silence while the ruling BJP has rushed to shield him from criticism. The united outcry of protest by the Opposition, led by the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi , is a strong signal of public opinion for the ruling party and India’s institutions, including the ECI, that appear complicit in a scheme that threatens the foundations of Indian democracy. What remains unexplained by the ECI and Mr. Kumar are malpractices in the Special Intensive Revision that could have the effect of subverting the popular will. Protestors on Sunday had arrived from all parts of India, and included people directly affected by the SIR across the country.

The protest reinforced Mr. Gandhi’s central role as the key challenger of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Gandhi, for all his faults, has been an uncompromising champion of constitutional values and pluralism in India. The BJP caricatured him, and even non-BJP voices had bought into the idea of Mr. Gandhi being a privileged dynast out of touch with the commoner. While his ancestry is a matter of fact, so is his tenacity. All Opposition parties mobilised for the protest, but the centrality of the Congress party was unmistakable. Mr. Gandhi has a special focus on subaltern classes to be included in positions of responsibility in the party. The Sunday protest was clearly the largest show of strength in recent memory. The manner in which the Congress coordinated with the wide spectrum of the Opposition, often involving rivals in States, also indicates a clear sense of purpose and pragmatism. The call for the restoration of institutional integrity is the need of the hour; but Mr. Gandhi must be careful not to misstate the nature of the crisis. In his well-reasoned call for accountability of the ECI, Mr. Gandhi ended up questioning the legitimacy of the previous election without providing any substantive basis for his allegations. He must remember that his emergence as the voice of the Opposition places on him the responsibility of being measured in his speeches and his steps.

articles.title: Cascading effect: On dams and land rights
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The bureaucratic impetus for the 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh purportedly comes from China’s aggressive development of a 60-GW mega-dam in Tibet , stoking anxieties among Indian authorities over ‘weaponised’ transboundary waters. Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh.

The Brahmaputra basin in Assam and Bangladesh receives most of its water from monsoon rains and tributaries downstream of the Tibetan Plateau, so China cannot straightforwardly control the river’s total flow through India. Yet since Chinese interventions would have greater consequences closer to the border, SUMP will need information about both the mega-dam’s operations and downstream inflows to plan its own operations, and Beijing has declined to share the former. SUMP thus faces many uncertainties at the outset. Despite India repeatedly raising the issue with China at the highest levels, headway has been limited to Beijing agreeing to share hydrological data on humanitarian grounds during emergencies. Planners have contemplated maintaining the SUMP reservoir at 70% to accommodate unexpected surges, but the level of protection possible if China supplies no advance warning remains unclear. This uncertainty is a thorn in the side of the government’s push against more legitimate resistance by Adi community members and civil rights groups. The need for the project does not excuse the state from following all the relevant laws and protections. The state cannot protect the nation’s needs by antagonising the nation’s people.

Despite India repeatedly raising the issue with China at the highest levels, headway has been limited to Beijing agreeing to share hydrological data on humanitarian grounds during emergencies. Planners have contemplated maintaining the SUMP reservoir at 70% to accommodate unexpected surges, but the level of protection possible if China supplies no advance warning remains unclear. This uncertainty is a thorn in the side of the government’s push against more legitimate resistance by Adi community members and civil rights groups. The need for the project does not excuse the state from following all the relevant laws and protections. The state cannot protect the nation’s needs by antagonising the nation’s people.

articles.title: Rains slow down across Andhra Pradesh after two days of havoc
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The rainfall activity, triggered by the Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’, has slowed down in Andhra Pradesh on Thursday, (November 5, 2026) after two days of havoc and leaving at least four perons dead, three in Bapatla district and one in Guntur district.

Between 8.30 a.m. and 2 p.m. on Thursday, only the district of SPSR Nellore recorded widespread moderate showers of around 55 mm. Other places in the districts of Tirupati, Anakapalli, Prakasam, recorded light showers till noon.

Light showers may continue on November 6, but after that, there may be a brief pause in the rainfall activity in the State. According to the India Meteorological Department’s forecast for the next seven days until November 12, the State may not see widespread rainfall, but it has said isolated heavy rainfall, at one or two places, in coastal A.P. is likely during the next seven days.

As per a release from the State Emergency Operations Centre of the Real Time Governance Society, reservoirs and drains are now stable, and that inflows are declining. Prakasam Barrage is discharging the same quantity as it is receiving. Thammileru and Budameru, which were rising on Wednesday, are now falling. Yerra Kalva, which had seen a sharp rise on Wednesday night, has also stabilised. Kondaveeti Vagu pump house is being operated to keep levels under control.
While the cyclone impact has largely subsided, the RTGS officials advised people in low-lying areas and near drains, canals and reservoirs to remain cautious.

On November 3 and 4, the districts of Palnadu, West Godavari, Bapatla, East Godavari, Kakinada, Eluru recorded very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall due to the cyclone. Except for Palnadu, which still has a deficit of 26.7%, the deficits in the other five districts have been covered after the reecnt spell of rains.

While the northern and Central parts of the State benefitted from the heavy rainfall caused by the two back-to-back cyclones of Arnab and Murasu, the region of Rayalaseema continues to wait for rain. Sri Sathy Sai is the worst hit, with 56% deficit, followed by Kurnool that has a deficit of 51.5%. Prakasam, which received good rain in the past two days, still has a deficit of 50.8%. Nandyal, Anantapur, YSR Kadapa and Annamayya have deficits between 40% and 50%, while Chittoor has a deficit of 32.4% and Tirupati 21.4%.

articles.title: Climate change increased tropical Cyclone Arnab’s damage by 33%: Study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Climate change increased the damage caused by the tropical Cyclone Arnab, which struck eastern India on October 28, by 33%, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in additional direct economic losses compared to a pre-industrial climate baseline, according to a new study.
ALSO WATCH Cyclone Arnab batters east coast: 5 dead in Andhra Pradesh, 17 Odisha districts affected
It added that the storm brought intense rain, peak 1-minute sustained winds of up to 202 kilometres per hour, and severe damage to infrastructure across Andhra Pradesh.
The study was carried out by researchers at the Imperial College London’s Grantham Institute and published on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

For their analysis, researchers used the Imperial College Storm Model (IRIS) to simulate Cyclone Arnab under current conditions (plus 1.3° Celsius above pre-industrial levels) versus a counterfactual climate without human-induced warming.
“Climate change increased Cyclone Arnab’s maximum wind speed by approximately 5%, and intensified its eyewall rainfall rate by 11% at landfall,” according to the study.

It also revealed that direct damage to physical assets in India was estimated to be 33% higher than it would have been in a pre-industrial climate baseline, attributing roughly 25% of the total economic damage directly to climate change.
ALSO WATCH Beyond Cyclone Arnab: can India tackle the growing cost of natural disasters? | Insight India

In a statement, Dr. Nathan Sparks, researcher at the Department of Physics, Imperial College London, said: “These findings are a powerful reminder of the price of inaction. The costs of climate change are not hypothetical future projections — they are hitting coastal communities in eastern India today.”

articles.title: Andhra local body polls: Clashes erupt between YSRCP, TDP groups in Kadapa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Amid ZPTC and MPTC elections, clashes broke out between YSRCP and TDP activists in several areas of Kadapa district on Thursday morning. Two groups of people have attacked each other with petrol bombs in Yerripalli village in Pulivendla mandal of the district.

According to sources, a quarrel started among the agents of YSRCP and TDP while sitting near a polling station in Yerripalli. The groups of both political parties have argued and exchanged harsh words. Meanwhile, some of them reportedly hurled petrol bombs. None were injured in the clash.

Speaking to The Hindu , Pulivendla Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Murali Nayak clarified, “The activists of both parties used firecrackers, which were brought to celebrate after victory, to attack each other. They took out petrol from their bikes to escalate the fight.”

“However, the police forces controlled them within five minutes. Such incidents took place near polling stations in R. Thummalapalli Parnapalli villages in Pulivendla mandal, but the police staff immediately calmed down the situation in these areas respectively,” he informed.

The clashes reportedly happened after Kadapa MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy toured those polling stations. The TDP workers have alleged that the YSRCP leader encouraged his party cadre to create violence with a fear of failure in ZPTC/ MPTC elections similar to Municipal polls.

Not only in Pulivendula, incidents of pelting stones were reported in Gundlakunta village in Jammalamadugu constituency and Nandalur village in Rajampeta division. The clashes were also witnessed in Chintarajupalli, Railway Kodur and Badvel areas.

District SP Shelke Nachiket Vishwanath visited the polling stations in Vemula mandal and inspected the security arrangements on the ground. He instructed the police personnel to remain vigilant and ensure that the elections are conducted in a peaceful and impartial manner.

The polling for 16 ZPTC and 55 MPTC constituencies commenced in the district at 7 am. Special security arrangements have been made at 167 highly sensitive, 134 sensitive and five problematic polling stations. Except few areas, the voting was peaceful with 48.92% turnout by 1 pm

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi was born in family of Prime Ministers, he is not after PM post but nation’s interests: Jagga Reddy

fullParagraphs: Reacting to Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s comment that Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi can never become the Prime Minister, Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) working president T. Jagga Reddy reminded that Mr. Gandhi was born in the family of Prime Ministers and he was not after the post but the nation’s interests.

Addressing a press conference at Gandhi Bhavan in Hyderabad on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), Mr. Jagga Reddy said the Prime Minister’s post had always been within the reach of the Nehru-Gandhi family and Mr. Rahul Gandhi could have become Prime Minister in 2004 and in 2009 itself had he wanted the position.

Mr. Rahul Gandhi is not after the Prime Minister’s position like others in the Bharatiya Janata (BJP), Mr. Jagga Reddy said adding that Telangana Congress was ready to take up Mr. Shah’s comments as a challenge and work towards winning all 17 Lok Sabha seats in the State in the next parliamentary elections.

Referring to the BJP’s invocation of Lord Ram in its political campaigns, he said Mahatma Gandhi had sung Raghupati Raghava Raja Ram during the freedom movement, at a time when neither the BJP nor its leaders Narendra Modi and Amit Shah was born.

He said the BJP was always busy claiming exclusive ownership of Lord Ram’s name, pointing out that the Congress and Mahatma Gandhi had invoked Ram in their public life long before the BJP came into existence. Mr. Jagga Reddy said the BJP had come to power and the Prime Minister had secured three terms by invoking Lord Ram’s name, but was not following the ideals and path shown by the Lord.

articles.title: Cheranalloor luxury car crash: court upholds teen’s bail, raps police and prosecution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Additional District and Sessions Court designated to try cases involving atrocities against women and children in Ernakulam, Keralam, on Thursday (November 5, 2026) dismissed the appeals seeking suspension of the bail granted to the 17-year-old involved in the Cheranalloor crash case that claimed a life, while coming down heavily on the police and prosecution.

Judge Kavitha Gangadharan questioned the very basis for the registration of the FIR against the teenager in conflict with law, pointing out that such registration is warranted only in offences carrying a punishment of seven years’ imprisonment or more. The multiple alterations made to the FIR also came in for criticism. The police were accused of showing scant regard for the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, with the court questioning the absence of the social background report mandated in cases involving juveniles. The court even read out the relevant provisions of the Act to the investigation officer, an Assistant Commissioner with the Crime Branch.
The court observed that the police are not expected to act beyond the law even under pressure. The judge also asked the prosecution to show reason for not imposing fine while dismissing the appeals.

Earlier, the court had directed the investigation officer to submit within an hour details of FIRs registered in the district or elsewhere in the State in connection with accidents involving juvenile drivers in which Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which prescribes punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder, had been invoked.

The court sought the data to append it to the order on the appeals filed by the prosecution and the family of the deceased against the bail granted to the teenager by the Juvenile Justice Board. She warned that the investigation officer would be held answerable if no FIRs had been registered elsewhere invoking BNS Section 105 in similar cases and if the provision had been invoked only in the present case. Though the officer submitted details of nine accident cases involving juveniles in the district, Section 105 had not been invoked in any of them.

The court was also critical of the investigating agency for filing the appeal against the bail in the wrong court instead of the court designated to try cases involving juveniles, the only such court in the district. The judge also sought to know from the prosecution whether it had any doubt that the Juvenile Justice Model Rules constituted the sole State government framework governing matters involving children in conflict with law.
Bhadrakeerthi R.J., daughter of the victim Jayabalakrishnan, expressed dismay over the verdict, which she said she “could not comprehend.”

“It was dramatic and full of twists. People of Keralam will have no faith in the courts any more. We were expecting a favourable verdict both from this court and the High Court, (which granted anticipatory bail to the judicial officer, the father of the juvenile accused). Issues that had never been raised until today were brought up by the court. However, we will continue our fight,” she said outside the court.

articles.title: Centre earmarks ₹2,814 crore to boost lithium, nickel processing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a ₹2,814-crore capital expenditure support scheme to establish domestic processing facilities for lithium and nickel, seeking to strengthen India’s critical mineral ecosystem and reduce import dependence. The scheme will remain in force for five years.

India’s domestic beneficiation and processing infrastructure for critical minerals remains limited, with commercial-scale operations constrained by high capital requirements, limited access to suitable technologies and inadequate availability of raw materials, the government said in a statement.
Union Minister for Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy said the scheme would strengthen domestic capabilities, boost manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports.

“It will benefit key sectors such as electronics, semiconductors, batteries, defence, heavy equipment and machinery, while supporting industries across the manufacturing value chain that utilise critical minerals,” he said in a social media post.
Under the scheme, the government will provide a capital subsidy of 30% of the investment required to establish four critical mineral processing plants — two each for lithium and nickel.
The minimum processing capacity will be 30,000 tonnes (30 kt) each for lithium and 50,000 tonnes (50 kt) each for nickel.
The subsidy will be capped at ₹500 crore per beneficiary for lithium projects and ₹900 crore per beneficiary for nickel facilities.

The four beneficiaries will be selected through a least-cost bidding process, with preference given to technically qualified applicants seeking the lowest capital expenditure support. Incentives will be disbursed in three tranches.

Industry body the Federation of Indian Mineral Industries (FIMI) welcomed the initiative, saying it could encourage fresh investments, increase domestic value addition and strengthen supply chains for battery manufacturing and other strategic industries.
However, it said that securing adequate raw materials would be critical to the scheme’s success.
“Ensuring a reliable supply of raw material through domestic mining and overseas sourcing will be equally important for the success of these processing facilities,” the industry body told The Hindu.
It also underlined the need to develop the entire value chain, from mining to processing and refining, to strengthen India’s long-term mineral security.
