articles.title: U.S. Midterm Election night agenda: When polls close and when to expect results
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: With voters deciding thousands of races across the United States on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), keeping track of the contests to watch and when results may arrive can be tricky.
Here is a rundown of the major races, hour by hour, and an indication of how long vote-counting may take.

4:30 a.m: The first polls of the night close in most of Indiana and Kentucky, but statewide winners will not be declared in either state until the last polls close at 5:30 a.m. Winners could be declared in the states’ easternmost congressional districts.
Key contests include competitive U.S. House races in Indiana’s 5th and Kentucky’s 6th congressional districts.

5:30 a.m: .All polls close in six states, including Georgia, South Carolina and Virginia, which typically complete most of their vote counting on election night. In the 2024 general election, vote counting in all three states reached the halfway mark during the 8 p.m. hour.

The counts were 90% complete at 8:51 a.m. in Georgia, 9:44 a.m. in South Carolina and 10:37 a.m. in Virginia. The Associated Press (AP) declared Republican Donald Trump the winner of Georgia’s competitive presidential contest at 11:28 a.m.
Most Florida polls also close at 5:30 a.m., including those in every competitive congressional district. Statewide winners will not be declared until polls close in the Central Time Zone at 6:30 a.m.

6:00 a.m.: Polls close in North Carolina, Ohio and West Virginia. All three states counted votes relatively quickly in 2024, reaching the halfway point at about 7:30 a.m. and roughly 90% by the 9:30 a.m. hour. The AP declared a winner in Ohio’s competitive 2024 U.S. Senate race at 9:57 a.m.

Key contests include U.S. Senate races in Georgia, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio; gubernatorial races in Georgia and Ohio; and U.S. House races in Florida, Indiana, South Carolina, Virginia, Ohio and North Carolina.
6:30 a.m.: This is prime time on election night, with polls fully or partially closing in nearly half the states, including Florida, Maine, New Hampshire and Pennsylvania.
Florida typically counts votes quickly, with results from much of the state beginning to come in during the 5:30 a.m. hour. In 2024, 90% of the vote had been counted by 6:37 a.m.

In 2024, vote counts in New Hampshire and Pennsylvania reached the halfway mark at 8:42 a.m. They reached 90% at 12:12 p.m. in New Hampshire and 11:18 a.m. in Pennsylvania. Maine did not reach the halfway mark until 12:54 a.m.

articles.title: Students blockade dozens of French schools and universities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Students blockaded dozens of high schools and universities across France on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) to maintain pressure on the government over education reforms as trade unions prepared for a nationwide strike.

After returning from a two-week autumn break, some students resumed their protest campaign on Monday (November 2), calling on the authorities to renovate dilapidated schools, reduce class sizes and create more university places.

Authorities said on Tuesday (November 3) that 48 out of France's 3,700 high schools were blocked amid tight security, including in Paris, Rennes and Lyon. The USL student union said 500 schools were blocked.
Fifty-one higher education institutions out of 184 were also disrupted, officials said.
The USL union denounced what it called heavy-handed tactics, with "young people pinned against walls and riot police units deployed" outside schools.
A union representative said the authorities appeared to want to blunt a new day of blockades when trade unions have called a nationwide strike.
"We don't even have the right to vote, we can't do anything, so this is our only way of expressing ourselves," a high school student in northwestern Paris said on condition of anonymity.
Thousands of students also marched in Paris and several other cities.
Education Minister Edouard Geffray spoke out against the action, saying students needed to study and prepare for exams.
"Preventing them from entering their school deprives them of a fundamental right: the right to an education," he said on X, adding that some staff members had "once again been subjected to violence".
In the northwestern city of Rennes, around 30 students blocked the Brequigny High School, one of the country's largest secondary schools.
Tensions quickly flared between students and the school administration.

articles.title: West Bengal's first relocated tigress captured on sojourn in Assam, returned to Buxa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The three-year-old tigress, who was recently relocated to West Bengal 's Buxa Tiger Reserve from Bihar , was captured on a foray into Assam and returned to West Bengal on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

The tigress, Dooars Rani (BTR-TF-1/ T-138), was released in Buxa on October 2 from Bihar’s Valmiki Tiger Reserve as part of the State’s first tiger relocation project. She crossed into Assam's Raimona National Park on Sunday (October 25, 2026) in search of habitat.

"On Tuesday, we tranquilised the tigress, caged her, and brought her back to Buxa. Initially we let her explore and captured her today only when she came close to human settlements. However, there is nothing to panic about now. The tigress is also safe and healthy," said Forest Minister Manoj Oraon. The minister has been present in Assam for the last four days to monitor the tigress.

According to the officials, the tigress crossed the Sankosh River and a road in Gosaigaon in Assam to enter Raimona looking for habitat. Her movement area was traced up to 25 km from the Bengal border.

Forest officials from Assam and West Bengal, along with a team from the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), initially decided to let her explore. "She is not the property of any government. It is the nature of tigers to explore. She will likely cross into Raimona or any other area again. Our team will continue to monitor her," said the minister.

On October 2, the tigress was translocated from Bihar’s Valmiki Tiger Reserve and released in the presence of Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. The CM said three more tigers would be released in Buxa over the next two months, and the initiative would not only help in conservation but also in boosting tourism.

Buxa was declared a tiger reserve in 1983, but there have been no reports of a tiger’s presence in the region of late. According to an official statement by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), the recovery of Buxa has been a sustained, science-based effort, and the Tiger Augmentation and Recovery Project, initiated by the Government of West Bengal with support from the NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India (WII), has been implemented collaboratively since 2018.

Forest officials say this new tigress from Bihar will be subjected to intensive post-release monitoring using a combination of telemetry, camera trapping, and field-based monitoring to assess her movement, adaptation, health, and behaviour.
